verses.zh: 有一个先知门徒的妻哀求以利沙说：「你仆人―我丈夫死了，他敬畏耶和华是你所知道的。现在有债主来，要取我两个儿子作奴仆。」
verses.en: Now a wife of one of the prophets[NOTE:1] appealed[NOTE:2] to Elisha for help, saying, “Your servant, my husband is dead. You know that your servant was a loyal follower of the Lord.[NOTE:3] Now the creditor is coming to take away my two boys to be his servants.”
notes: Heb “a wife from among the wives of the sons of the prophets.”
Or “cried out.”
Heb “your servant feared the Lord.” “Fear” refers here to obedience and allegiance, the products of healthy respect for the Lord’s authority.

verses.zh: 以利沙问她说：「我可以为你做甚么呢？你告诉我，你家里有甚么？」她说：「婢女家中除了一瓶油之外，没有甚么。」
verses.en: Elisha said to her, “What can I do for you? Tell me, what do you have in the house?” She answered, “Your servant has nothing in the house except a small jar of olive oil.”

verses.zh: 以利沙说：「你去，向你众邻舍借空器皿，不要少借；
verses.en: He said, “Go and ask all your neighbors for empty containers.[NOTE:1] Get as many as you can.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “Go, ask for containers from outside, from all your neighbors, empty containers.”
Heb “Do not borrow just a few.”

verses.zh: 回到家里，关上门，你和你儿子在里面将油倒在所有的器皿里，倒满了的放在一边。」
verses.en: Go and close the door behind you and your sons. Pour the olive oil into all the containers;[NOTE:1] set aside each one when you have filled it.”
notes: Heb “all these vessels.”

verses.zh: 于是，妇人离开以利沙去了，关上门，自己和儿子在里面；儿子把器皿拿来，她就倒油。
verses.en: So she left him and closed the door behind her and her sons. As they were bringing the containers to her, she was pouring the olive oil.

verses.zh: 器皿都满了，她对儿子说：「再给我拿器皿来。」儿子说：「再没有器皿了。」油就止住了。
verses.en: When the containers were full, she said to one of her sons,[NOTE:1] “Bring me another container.” But he answered her, “There are no more.” Then the olive oil stopped flowing.
notes: Heb “to her son.”

verses.zh: 妇人去告诉神人，神人说：「你去卖油还债，所剩的你和你儿子可以靠着度日。」
verses.en: She went and told the prophet.[NOTE:1] He said, “Go, sell the olive oil. Repay your creditor, and then you and your sons can live off the rest of the profit.”
notes: Heb “man of God” (also in vv. 16, 22, 25, 27 [twice]).

verses.zh: 一日，以利沙走到书念，在那里有一个大户的妇人强留他吃饭。此后，以利沙每从那里经过就进去吃饭。
verses.en: One day Elisha traveled to Shunem, where a prominent[NOTE:1] woman lived. She insisted that he stop for a meal.[NOTE:2] So whenever he was passing through, he would stop in there for a meal.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “great,” perhaps “wealthy.”
Or “she urged him to eat some food.”
Or “he would turn aside there to eat some food.”

verses.zh: 妇人对丈夫说：「我看出那常从我们这里经过的是圣洁的神人。
verses.en: She said to her husband, “Look, I’m sure[NOTE:1] that the man who regularly passes through here is a very special prophet.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “I know.”
Heb “holy man of God.”

verses.zh: 我们可以为他在墙上盖一间小楼，在其中安放床榻、桌子、椅子、灯台，他来到我们这里，就可以住在其间。」
verses.en: Let’s make a small, private upper room[NOTE:1] and furnish it with[NOTE:2] a bed, table, chair, and lamp. When he visits us, he can stay there.”
notes: Heb “a small upper room of a wall.” According to HALOT 832 s.v. עֲלִיָּה, this refers to “a fully walled upper room.”
Heb “and let’s put there for him.”

verses.zh: 一日，以利沙来到那里，就进了那楼躺卧。
verses.en: One day Elisha[NOTE:1] came for a visit; he went[NOTE:2] into the upper room and rested.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “he”; the referent (Elisha) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “turned aside.”
Or “slept there.”

verses.zh: 以利沙吩咐仆人基哈西说：「你叫这书念妇人来。」他就把妇人叫了来，妇人站在以利沙面前。
verses.en: He told his servant Gehazi, “Ask the Shunammite woman to come here.”[NOTE:1] So he did so and she came to him.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “Call for this Shunammite woman.”
Heb “and he called for her and she stood before him.”

verses.zh: 以利沙吩咐仆人说：「你对她说：你既为我们费了许多心思，可以为你做甚么呢？你向王或元帅有所求的没有？」她回答说：「我在我本乡安居无事。」
verses.en: Elisha said to Gehazi,[NOTE:1] “Tell her, ‘Look, you have treated us with such great respect.[NOTE:2] What can I do for you? Can I put in a good word for you with the king or the commander of the army?’” She replied, “I’m quite secure.”[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “he said to him.”

Heb “you have turned trembling to us with all this trembling.” The exaggerated language is probably idiomatic. The point seems to be that she has taken great pains or gone out of her way to be kind to them. Her concern was a sign of her respect for the prophetic office.
Heb “Among my people I am living.” This answer suggests that she has security within the context of her family.

verses.zh: 以利沙对仆人说：「究竟当为她做甚么呢？」基哈西说：「她没有儿子，她丈夫也老了。」
verses.en: So he asked Gehazi,[NOTE:1] “What can I do for her?” Gehazi replied, “She has no son, and her husband is old.”
notes: Heb “and he said.”

verses.zh: 以利沙说：「再叫她来。」于是叫了她来，她就站在门口。
verses.en: Elisha told him, “Ask her to come here.”[NOTE:1] So he did so[NOTE:2] and she came and stood in the doorway.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “Call for her.”
Heb “and he called her.”
Heb “and he called for her and she stood in the door.”

verses.zh: 以利沙说：「明年到这时候，你必抱一个儿子。」她说：「神人，我主啊，不要那样欺哄婢女。」
verses.en: He said, “About this time next year[NOTE:1] you will be holding a son.” She said, “No, my master! O prophet, do not lie to your servant!”
notes: Heb “at this appointed time, at the time [when it is] reviving.” For a discussion of the second phrase see M. Cogan and H. Tadmor, II Kings (AB), 57.

verses.zh: 妇人果然怀孕，到了那时候，生了一个儿子，正如以利沙所说的。
verses.en: The woman did conceive, and at the specified time the next year she gave birth to a son, just as Elisha had told her.

verses.zh: 孩子渐渐长大，一日到他父亲和收割的人那里，
verses.en: The boy grew and one day he went out to see his father who was with the harvest workers.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “to his father, to the harvesters.”

verses.zh: 他对父亲说：「我的头啊，我的头啊！」他父亲对仆人说：「把他抱到他母亲那里。」
verses.en: He said to his father, “My head! My head!” His father[NOTE:1] told a servant, “Carry him to his mother.”
notes: Heb “He”; the referent (the boy’s father) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 仆人抱去，交给他母亲；孩子坐在母亲的膝上，到晌午就死了。
verses.en: So he picked him up and took him to his mother. He sat on her lap[NOTE:1] until noon and then died.
notes: Heb “knees.”

verses.zh: 他母亲抱他上了楼，将他放在神人的床上，关上门出来，
verses.en: She went up and laid him down on the prophet’s[NOTE:1] bed. She shut the door behind her and left.
notes: Heb “man of God’s.”

verses.zh: 呼叫她丈夫说：「你叫一个仆人给我牵一匹驴来，我要快快地去见神人，就回来。」
verses.en: She called to her husband, “Send me one of the servants and one of the donkeys, so I can go see the prophet quickly and then return.”

verses.zh: 丈夫说：「今日不是月朔，也不是安息日，你为何要去见他呢？」妇人说：「平安无事。」
verses.en: He said, “Why do you want to go see him today? It is not the new moon[NOTE:1] or the Sabbath.” She said, “Everything’s fine.”[NOTE:2]
notes: The new moon was a time of sacrifice and special feasts (Num 28:14; 1 Sam 20:5). Apparently it was a convenient time to visit a prophet. See M. Cogan and H. Tadmor, II Kings (AB), 57.
Heb “peace.”

verses.zh: 于是备上驴，对仆人说：「你快快赶着走，我若不吩咐你，就不要迟慢。」
verses.en: She saddled the donkey and told her servant, “Lead on.[NOTE:1] Do not stop unless I say so.”[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “lead [the donkey on] and go.”
Heb “do not restrain for me the riding unless I say to you.”

verses.zh: 妇人就往迦密山去见神人。神人远远地看见她，对仆人基哈西说：「看哪，书念的妇人来了！
verses.en: So she went to visit[NOTE:1] the prophet at Mount Carmel. When he[NOTE:2] saw her at a distance, he said to his servant Gehazi, “Look, it’s the Shunammite woman.
notes: Heb “went and came.”
Heb “the man of God.” The phrase has been replaced by the relative pronoun “he” in the translation for stylistic reasons.

verses.zh: 你跑去迎接她，问她说：你平安吗？你丈夫平安吗？孩子平安吗？」她说：「平安。」
verses.en: Now, run to meet her and ask her, ‘Are you well? Are your husband and the boy well?’” She told Gehazi,[NOTE:1] “Everything’s fine.”
notes: Heb “she said.” The narrator streamlines the story at this point, omitting any reference to Gehazi running to meet her and asking her the questions.

verses.zh: 妇人上了山，到神人那里，就抱住神人的脚。基哈西前来要推开她，神人说：「由她吧！因为她心里愁苦，耶和华向我隐瞒，没有指示我。」
verses.en: But when she reached the prophet on the mountain, she grabbed hold of his feet. Gehazi came near to push her away, but the prophet said, “Leave her alone, for she is very upset.[NOTE:1] The Lord has kept the matter hidden from me; he didn’t tell me about it.”
notes: Heb “her soul [i.e., ‘disposition’] is bitter.”

verses.zh: 妇人说：「我何尝向我主求过儿子呢？我岂没有说过，不要欺哄我吗？」
verses.en: She said, “Did I ask my master for a son? Didn’t I say, ‘Don’t mislead me?’”

verses.zh: 以利沙吩咐基哈西说：「你束上腰，手拿我的杖前去；若遇见人，不要向他问安；人若向你问安，也不要回答；要把我的杖放在孩子脸上。」
verses.en: Elisha[NOTE:1] told Gehazi, “Tuck your robes into your belt, take my staff,[NOTE:2] and go! Don’t stop to exchange greetings with anyone![NOTE:3] Place my staff on the child’s face.”
notes: Heb “he”; the referent (Elisha) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “take my staff in your hand.”
Heb “If you meet a man, do not greet him with a blessing; if a man greets you with a blessing, do not answer.”

verses.zh: 孩子的母亲说：「我指着永生的耶和华，又敢在你面前起誓，我必不离开你。」于是以利沙起身，随着她去了。
verses.en: The mother of the child said, “As certainly as the Lord lives and as you live, I will not leave you.” So Elisha[NOTE:1] got up and followed her back.
notes: Heb “he”; the referent (Elisha) has been specified in the translation for clarity. The referent must be Elisha here, since the following verse makes it clear that Gehazi had gone on ahead of them.

verses.zh: 基哈西先去，把杖放在孩子脸上，却没有声音，也没有动静。基哈西就迎着以利沙回来，告诉他说：「孩子还没有醒过来。」
verses.en: Now Gehazi went on ahead of them. He placed the staff on the child’s face, but there was no sound or response. When he came back to Elisha[NOTE:1] he told him, “The child did not wake up.”
notes: Heb “to meet him.”

verses.zh: 以利沙来到，进了屋子，看见孩子死了，放在自己的床上。
verses.en: When Elisha arrived at the house, there was[NOTE:1] the child lying dead on his bed.
notes: Heb “look.”

verses.zh: 他就关上门，只有自己和孩子在里面，他便祈祷耶和华，
verses.en: He went in by himself and closed the door.[NOTE:1] Then he prayed to the Lord.
notes: Heb “and closed the door behind the two of them.”

verses.zh: 上床伏在孩子身上，口对口，眼对眼，手对手；既伏在孩子身上，孩子的身体就渐渐温和了。
verses.en: He got up on the bed and spread his body out over[NOTE:1] the boy; he put his mouth on the boy’s[NOTE:2] mouth, his eyes over the boy’s eyes, and the palms of his hands against the boy’s palms. As he bent down across him, the boy’s skin[NOTE:3] grew warm.
notes: Heb “he went up and lay down over.”
Heb “his” (also in the next two clauses).
Or perhaps, “body”; Heb “flesh.”

verses.zh: 然后他下来，在屋里来往走了一趟，又上去伏在孩子身上，孩子打了七个喷嚏，就睁开眼睛了。
verses.en: Elisha[NOTE:1] went back and walked around in the house.[NOTE:2] Then he got up on the bed again[NOTE:3] and bent down over him. The child sneezed seven times and opened his eyes.
notes: Heb “he”; the referent (Elisha) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “and he returned and went into the house, once here and once there.”
Heb “and he went up.”

verses.zh: 以利沙叫基哈西说：「你叫这书念妇人来」；于是叫了她来。以利沙说：「将你儿子抱起来。」
verses.en: Elisha[NOTE:1] called to Gehazi and said, “Get the Shunammite woman.” So he did so[NOTE:2] and she came to him. He said to her, “Take your son.”
notes: Heb “he”; the referent (Elisha) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “and he called for her.”

verses.zh: 妇人就进来，在以利沙脚前俯伏于地，抱起她儿子出去了。
verses.en: She came in, fell at his feet, and bowed down. Then she picked up her son and left.

verses.zh: 以利沙又来到吉甲，那地正有饥荒。先知门徒坐在他面前，他吩咐仆人说：「你将大锅放在火上，给先知门徒熬汤。」
verses.en: Now Elisha went back to Gilgal, while there was a famine in the land. Some of the prophets were visiting him[NOTE:1] and he told his servant, “Put the big pot on the fire[NOTE:2] and boil some stew for the prophets.”[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “the sons of the prophets were sitting before him.”
The words “the fire” are added for clarification.
Heb “sons of the prophets.”

verses.zh: 有一个人去到田野掐菜，遇见一棵野瓜藤，就摘了一兜野瓜回来，切了搁在熬汤的锅中，因为他们不知道是甚么东西；
verses.en: Someone went out to the field to gather some herbs and found a wild vine.[NOTE:1] He picked some of its fruit,[NOTE:2] enough to fill up the fold of his robe. He came back, cut it up, and threw the slices[NOTE:3] into the stew pot, not knowing they were harmful.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “a vine of the field.”
Heb “[some] of the gourds of the field.”
Heb “he came and cut [them up].”

The Hebrew text reads, “for they did not know” (יָדָעוּ, yadaʿu) but some emend the final shureq (וּ, indicating a third plural subject) to holem vav (וֹ, a third masculine singular pronominal suffix on a third singular verb) and read “for he did not know it.” Perhaps it is best to omit the final vav as dittographic (note the vav at the beginning of the next verb form) and read simply, “for he did not know.” See M. Cogan and H. Tadmor, II Kings (AB), 59.

verses.zh: 倒出来给众人吃，吃的时候，都喊叫说：「神人哪，锅中有致死的毒物！」所以众人不能吃了。
verses.en: The stew was poured out[NOTE:1] for the men to eat. When they ate some of the stew, they cried out, “Death is in the pot, O prophet!” They could not eat it.
notes: Heb “and they poured out [the stew].” The plural subject is probably indefinite.

verses.zh: 以利沙说：「拿点面来」，就把面撒在锅中，说：「倒出来，给众人吃吧！」锅中就没有毒了。
verses.en: He said, “Get some flour.” Then he threw it into the pot and said, “Now pour some out for the men so they may eat.”[NOTE:1] There was no longer anything harmful in the pot.
notes: Or “and let them eat.”

verses.zh: 有一个人从巴力・沙利沙来，带着初熟大麦做的饼二十个，并新穗子，装在口袋里送给神人。神人说：「把这些给众人吃。」
verses.en: Now a man from Baal Shalisha brought some food for the prophet[NOTE:1]—20 loaves of bread made from the firstfruits of the barley harvest, as well as fresh ears of grain.[NOTE:2] Elisha[NOTE:3] said, “Set it before the people so they may eat.”
notes: Heb “man of God.”
On the meaning of the word צִקְלוֹן (tsiqlon), “ear of grain,” see HALOT 148 s.v. בָּצֵק and M. Cogan and H. Tadmor, II Kings (AB), 59.
Heb “he”; the referent (Elisha) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 仆人说：「这一点岂可摆给一百人吃呢？」以利沙说：「你只管给众人吃吧！因为耶和华如此说，众人必吃了，还剩下。」
verses.en: But his attendant said, “How can I feed a hundred men with this?”[NOTE:1] He replied, “Set it before the people so they may eat, for this is what the Lord has said, ‘They will eat and have some left over.’”[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “How can I set this before a hundred men?”
The verb forms are infinitives absolute (Heb “eating and leaving over”) and have to be translated in light of the context.

verses.zh: 仆人就摆在众人面前，他们吃了，果然还剩下，正如耶和华所说的。
verses.en: So he set it before them; they ate and had some left over, just as in the Lord’s message.

READING CYCLE THREE (see
"Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT THE PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own
interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation.
You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects. Compare your subject divisions with the five translations
above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation.
Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

- First paragraph

- Second paragraph

- Etc.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- These miracle stories are similar to the miracles of Elijah.

- They are recorded to illustrate the "double portion" of Elijah's spirit on Elisha. Elisha did twice as many recorded miracles as Elijah.

- These miracles show YHWH's concern and care for ordinary people.

- even non-Israelite people

- rich and poor

- 2 Kings 4:27 shows that prophets did not have full knowledge about all things. It was a selective revelation.

- 2 Kings. 4:34-35 is an example of healing/restoration in stages (i.e., Jesus healing blindness in stages,
i.e., Mark 8:23-25).
This would be a faith test for the prophet.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: 4:1-7

1Now a certain woman of the wives of the sons of the prophets cried out to Elisha,
"Your servant my husband is dead, and you know that your servant feared the
Lord; and the creditor has come to take my two children to be his
slaves." 2Elisha said to her, "What shall I do for you? Tell me, what do you have in
the house?" And she said, "Your maidservant has nothing in the house except a jar of oil."
3Then he said, "Go, borrow vessels at large for yourself from all your neighbors,
even empty vessels; do not get a few. 4And you shall go in and shut the door behind
you and your sons, and pour out into all these vessels, and you shall set aside what is full."
5So she went from him and shut the door behind her and her sons; they were bringing
the vessels to her and she poured. 6When the vessels were full, she said to her son,
"Bring me another vessel." And he said to her, "There is not one vessel more." And the oil stopped.
7Then she came and told the man of God. And he said, "Go, sell the oil and pay your
debt, and you and your sons can live on the rest."

4:1 "the wives" Prophets were usually married. The rabbis viewed marriage as a requirement. Notice YHWH's
repeated command to be fruitful and multiply (i.e., Gen. 1:28; 9:1,7).

SPECIAL TOPIC: CELIBACY

▣ "the sons of the prophets" Originally the prophets lived in communal groups (i.e., 1 Sam. 10:5,10;
19:20; 2 Kgs. 2:3; 4:1,38; 5:22). They were unconnected to the later court prophets.

▣ "feared the Lord" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: FEAR (OT).

▣ "my two children to be his slaves" The confiscation of the children as servants was one way to pay a debt
(i.e., Exod. 21:7; Neh. 5:5). This practice of Hebrew servitude is discussed in Lev. 25:39-55; Deut. 15:12-15.

For a good brief discussion on "Israelite slaves" see Roland deVaux, Ancient Israel, pp. 80-90.

4:2 "a jar of oil" Olive oil was a basic part of the Mediterranean diet. This is similar to Elijah's miracle in 1 Kgs. 17:14-16.

The word "jar" (BDB 692) occurs only here. Some see it as a flask for pouring or anointing.

4:4 "shut the door" Elisha did several acts behind closed doors (i.e., 2 Kgs. 4:4,5,33; 9:3,10). Why?

- People may not understand the uniqueness of the event and its background.

- It could promote a "give me a miracle" mentality.

- Not all of YHWH's actions are for public knowledge (i.e., "do not cast your pearls before swine").

4:7 "the man of God" This was a way of designating a speaker for YHWH (i.e., v. 9). This title first appears in

4:10 "the upper chamber" Small rooms (i.e., a walled room) on the flat roofs were common in the ANE. They

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible for your own
interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation.
You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of
the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

- Could children be taken as a payment for debt?

- What is unusual about v. 9?

- What was the significance of Elisha's staff? Why did the staff not revive the boy?

- Why did Elisha advocate secrecy in his prophetic actions (vv. 5,33)?

- What did the seven "sneezes" represent?

- What was the purpose of the two miracle stories at the close of the chapter?
